title: [GCE Discovery] Correcly handle large zones with 500 or more instances

timeline.body:
discovery gce plugin has some issues while running in large pools of vms instances.

this pr attempts to solve it.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/83783

Thanks for the PR @cdmbr. Looks like you're still actively working on it so I've marked it as a draft for now. Please ping when it's ready for review. The following command will enable CI on your branch:

@elasticsearchmachine ok to test

thanks for the return @DaveCTurner !

I was just doing some lint fixes (forgot to run spotless 😅), but it seems that it is all set. I'm marking it as ready for review.

Question: when it merges, will it be back-ported for all previous versions ?

I believe it would be better to use a standard `ArrayList` here. `LinkedList` is very rarely outperforms `ArrayList` due to its bad speed of traversal and the lack memory locality. See https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/JdkObsolete#LinkedList

reply.body: I used linkedlist here due to its O(1) in insertions ... But for traversals is not that good ...

timeline.body:
I believe `setPageToken` returns the correct list request, so we should be able to chain it. WDYT about
```java
Compute.Instances.List list = client().instances().list(project, zoneId).setPageToken(nextPageToken);
```

I believe question marks are not allowed in filenames on Windows, hence the Windows tests fail. 

What do you think about replacing the question mark with `%3F` from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding and then make sure the question mark gets encoded in `GceMockUtils#readJsonResponse`?

```java
String mockFileName = Strings.replace(url, urlRoot, "")
            .replace("?", "%3F")
```

timeline.body: We should assert that we get the expected `TransportAddress` values here.

reply.body: @fcofdez No tests in this class does this assertion. The tests only make sure that we have the expected number of distinct hosts ... Do we really need to make this assertion here (also by hardcoding the expected mocked hosts) ? Maybe checking if the transport address parsing is correct should be done in another test class.
It's to ensure that we get the expected results from the different responses.

I understand your point, but having the distinct count of the the transport addresses here is not enough (2 mocked resources, 1 instance each) ?

Maybe for sake of sanity, in the size assertion we could convert dynamicHosts list to a set (TransportAddress has an equals impl) and check if there's no duplicated addresses there ....

But I've made the new assertions as you pointed out ... plz take another look @fcofdez

timeline.body: @cdmbr Thanks for the contribution, it looks good, I've left a comment around the test that I think it should be addressed.
